context: It now speaks. Though it is made of more than a thousand souls, it has one voice and says "I".

note: Many just rulers speak as one person. Justice is the same in all of them, and Dante held that the world should likewise be united under one just ruler.
The two virtues of a good ruler. The souls speak of their life on earth as if it had been a single reign.
The order of angels called Thrones, who are said in Paradiso 9 to be mirrors that reflect God's judgments to the heavens below.

context: The question Dante has carried since he saw Virgil and the great pagans there: how can it be just to shut out good people who never had the chance to believe?

quote: a falcon emerging from its hood
note: A hunting falcon was kept hooded on the fist. When the hood came off, it roused, shook its head and beat its wings, eager to fly.
The eagle was the standard carried before the Roman legions, and later the emblem of the empire.

God as the architect of the universe, drawing its outer limit with a pair of compasses. The picture comes from the Book of Proverbs, where Wisdom is present when God sets a circle on the face of the deep.
God's own thought, the plan of all that he could make, identified with the Son. No created universe can hold all of it, so no created mind can understand all of God.

context: Even the highest creature could not see all of God by his own power. He would not wait for the light of grace that would have completed him, and so fell "unripe".

note: The heart of the answer. God's justice has a bottom, as the sea does, but human sight is too weak to reach it. Not seeing it is no proof that it is absent.
The great river of India, which for Dante's Europe was the far eastern edge of the known world.

quote: Who are you to sit in judgment
note: An echo of Saint Paul in the Letter to the Romans: "Who are you, a man, to answer back to God?"
A span is the width of a spread hand, about nine inches.

quote: If Scripture were not over you
note: The Bible states that God is just. Reason on its own could argue the question forever. A Christian has to start from that given point.
God's will. It is not measured against some outside standard of justice: it is the standard. A thing is just to the degree that it agrees with it.
Dante hears the song but cannot follow its words. The eagle makes that the lesson: he can know God's judgment is there without understanding it.
Before Christ, the faith in question is that of the Hebrews who believed in a savior to come. The rule sounds final, but the next canto shows two souls no one would expect to find under it.

From the Sermon on the Mount: "Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven." In the Italian, the name Cristo ends three lines in a row here. Throughout the poem Dante rhymes it only with itself.

Any pagan from a far country, like the Persians three lines below. In the Gospel of Matthew, Christ says that the pagans of Nineveh will rise at the judgment and condemn those who heard him and did not repent.
The saved and the damned at the Last Judgment, divided like sheep from goats in the Gospel of Matthew.
The record of every person's deeds, opened at the Last Judgment in the Book of Revelation.

The roll of bad Christian kings is an acrostic. In the Italian, three stanzas begin with L, the next three with V, which was also the letter U, and the next three with E. They spell LUE, a word for plague.

context: In 1304 he invaded Bohemia, the kingdom of his brother-in-law, and laid it waste. In 1300 that is still to be written in the book.

note: Bohemia, of which Prague was the capital.

context: To pay for his wars in Flanders he lowered the amount of precious metal in the French coinage, which ruined many. He died in 1314 after a hunting accident, when a wild boar brought down his horse.

note: The border wars between England and Scotland, which began in the 1290s under Edward I of England and went on through Dante's lifetime.
Usually identified as Ferdinand IV of Castile, who reigned from 1295 to 1312.
Wenceslaus II, king of Bohemia until 1305, the same king whose realm Albert will ravage. Purgatorio 7 also calls him a man sunk in lust and idleness.

context: He was lame, and he held the empty title of king of Jerusalem. The letters are Roman numerals: his good qualities add up to one, his bad ones to a thousand. The one is usually said to be his generosity.

quote: him who guards the Island of Fire
note: Frederick II of Aragon, king of Sicily from 1296 to 1337. The fire is Mount Etna. In the Aeneid, Aeneas's father Anchises dies in Sicily, at Drepanum, now Trapani.
Either his misdeeds are so many that only shorthand will fit them on the page, or the man is too paltry to be given more room.
Frederick's uncle James, king of Majorca, and his brother James II, king of Aragon. Majorca and Aragon are the two crowns, and the nation is the royal house of Aragon.
Two kings, not one: Denis of Portugal, who reigned from 1279 to 1325, and the king of Norway, in 1300 Haakon V. Dante gives no reasons, and it is not clear what he held against them.
Stephen Uros II, king of Serbia from 1282 to 1321. Rascia was an old name for his kingdom. He struck coins that copied the Venetian silver grosso but contained less silver.
Hungary's old royal line died out in 1301, and after some years of struggle the crown went to Charles Robert of Anjou. He was the son of Charles Martel, the young king Dante meets in Paradiso 8.

A small kingdom in the Pyrenees. Its queen, Joan, was married to the king of France, and at her death in 1305 it passed to the French royal house. The hills that should have guarded it are the mountains on the French side.

The two chief cities of Cyprus. Their "beast" is the island's king in 1300, Henry II of Lusignan. A small king, but he keeps pace with the larger beasts just named, and his island's misery shows what is coming to the rest.
